# Homepage phone tour video (#2012) — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A ~40 s silent phone recording of the app, per theme, shown on the project homepage in a CSS phone frame with a scene list that follows the video; regenerated by one command.

**Architecture:** `frontend/scripts/screenshots/tour.mjs` drives Playwright against the dev stack (`:4200`), records five scenes at true 2x and encodes MP4/WebM/poster plus `tour-scenes.json` into `docs/homepage/`. The helpers it shares with `shots.mjs` move into `lib.mjs`. `docs/homepage/index.html` gets a `#tour` section; its inline script highlights the current scene on `timeupdate` and seeks on tap.

**Tech Stack:** Node 22 ESM, `@playwright/test` Chromium, ffmpeg (libx264, libvpx-vp9), cwebp, static HTML/CSS/JS.

**Spec:** [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-2012-homepage-phone-tour-design.md](../specs/2026-11-03-2012-homepage-phone-tour-design.md)

## Global Constraints

- Branch `feature/2012-homepage-phone-tour` off `develop`; spec committed. Commit format `type(#2012): summary`, no attribution. PR into `develop`, body `Closes #2012`.
- Scripts are outside `ng lint`; keep them Prettier-clean anyway (`npx prettier --check scripts/screenshots/*.mjs` from `frontend/`), like the existing ones.
- The demo account ends every run as it started (19 feeds). After an aborted run: `node --env-file=.env.screenshots scripts/screenshots/podcast-setup.mjs teardown`.
- Each MP4 under 4.5 MB.
- The handed-over script (the other session's scratchpad `tour.mjs`) is the starting point; its solved pitfalls (spec, "Recording") stay.

### Task 2: `tour.mjs` with a reliable reader warm-up

**Files:** Create `frontend/scripts/screenshots/tour.mjs` from the handed-over script.

- [ ] Bare `import { chromium } from '@playwright/test'` instead of `createRequire`; paths from `import.meta.url` like `shots.mjs`; helpers from `lib.mjs`.
- [ ] Replace `waitForArticle` with `waitForReaderBody(page, title, timeout)`: `page.waitForFunction` until `app-reader-view h1.title` has the tapped title and then either `app-reader-view app-article-content` has `innerText.length >= 1200` (resolves with that length) or a fallback (`.reader-fallback, .reader-fallback-quiet, .body-error`) is present (resolves with 0). A timeout counts as 0. `warmReadableTitles` keeps titles with a length ≥ 1200; `readerScene` waits on the same function.
- [ ] `readerScene` stays robust if a warmed article still falls back on camera: after the tap, if the wait returns 0 within 5 s, go back and tap the next on-screen warmed title (at most twice).
- [ ] Verify: run `TOUR_OUT=<scratch> … tour.mjs light`, then `dark`; the warm-up log shows the same articles readable across both runs with stable lengths. Account at 19 feeds afterwards.
- [ ] Commit `feat(#2012): record the homepage phone tour with tour.mjs`.

### Task 4: The `#tour` section on the homepage

**Files:** Modify `docs/homepage/index.html`.

- [ ] Markup after `.hero`: `<section id="tour">` with `h2` "See it in action", a one-sentence lede, a `.tour` grid of `.phone-frame` (bezel, island, `.screen` holding two `<video>`s: `light-only` with `preload="metadata"`, `dark-only` with `preload="none"`, both `muted playsinline controls width="780" height="1520"`, poster, WebM then MP4 `<source>`) and an `<ol class="tour-scenes">` with one `<li data-seconds>` per scene (label in `<strong>`, copy in `<span>`) from `tour-scenes.json`'s light list.
- [ ] CSS beside the page's other section styles, tokens only: frame proportions from `frame.mjs` scaled to the column width, `aria-current` highlight with `--accent`, one column under the page's existing 900 px breakpoint.
- [ ] Script in the page's existing `<script>`: the visible video is the one whose `offsetParent` is non-null; on `timeupdate` set `aria-current="true"` on the latest scene with `seconds <= currentTime` (per theme, the dark list's seconds come from a `data-dark-seconds` attribute); a click on a scene sets `currentTime` and plays. Scenes are buttons inside the `<li>` for keyboard access.
- [ ] Verify in the browser pane (file URL of the checkout): light and dark via the page's theme switch, desktop and 390 px widths, playback highlights scenes in order, tap seeks.
- [ ] Commit `feat(#2012): homepage tour section with a phone frame and scene list`.
